Comfort in Hard Times: Hard days come to everyone sooner or later. The verses in this part were chosen for those days, the times of grief, worry, illness or loss. Here you will meet the shepherd of Psalm 23 and the refuge of Psalm 46. Take each puzzle at your own pace, and let the words keep you company.
Peace for an Anxious Heart: Worry has a way of filling the mind, especially late at night. This part gathers verses about calm trust, honest prayer and restful sleep. Among them are the gentle teaching of Matthew 6 and the old blessing of Numbers 6. Settle into a comfortable chair, take a slow breath, and let each verse appear one letter at a time.
Hope That Does Not Fade: Hope in the Bible is more than wishing things were different. The verses in this part look ahead with steady confidence: to mercy that does not run out, to the empty tomb in Matthew 28, and to life with God that death cannot end. Some, like Lamentations 3, come from a place of deep sorrow, and their hope shines all the brighter for it.
Strength & Courage: Courage is not the same as having no fear. Many verses in this part were first spoken to people facing something hard, such as Joshua at the start of a great task, or the weary listeners of Isaiah 40. Again and again they point to a strength that comes from God rather than from ourselves. They are worth reading twice.
Faith & Trust: What does trusting God look like on an ordinary Tuesday? The verses in this part offer some answers, from the wise sayings of Proverbs 3 to the plain, searching words of Micah 6. Others speak of friendship, gentle words and love. Some will be old favorites, and a few may surprise you.
Love, Joy & Praise: This part is full of gladness. You will find psalms of thanks and praise, the well-loved chapter on love in 1 Corinthians 13, and many verses about God's love for people. Some of these psalms call for singing, so feel free to read your finished answers aloud. It may brighten your day.
Christmas: Good Tidings of Great Joy: Here the book turns to Christmas, a part to enjoy in that season or any time of year. These verses follow the story: the prophets' promises, the angel's visit to Mary, the manger, the shepherds and the angels, and the wise men who followed the star. The opening of John 1 is here too. May these verses bring you a little of that great joy.
